description: Curated MoodJournal semantic evaluation cases for Phase 4.

cases.description: A generally steady week with ordinary daily variation.

journal_entries.notes: A normal workday. I cooked dinner and relaxed afterward.
I was busy but handled my tasks without much stress.
I enjoyed talking with a friend after work.
A quiet day at home with time to recharge.

expected_facts: Mood remains generally stable across the week
The entries include ordinary work, social, and rest activities
forbidden_claims: The user experienced a mental-health crisis
The user has a diagnosed mental-health condition

cases.description: Stress early in the week gives way to relief and optimism.

journal_entries.notes: Work felt overwhelming and I slept poorly.
I completed an important task and felt relieved.
I felt calmer and enjoyed a walk outside.
I rested and felt optimistic about next week.

expected_facts: The week begins with stress
Mood generally improves over the week
forbidden_claims: The user has depression
The user is taking medication

cases.description: Energy and mood decline as workload increases.

journal_entries.notes: I started the week energized and prepared.
Deadlines started piling up and I felt tense.
I was tired and had trouble focusing at work.
I felt drained and worried about the coming week.

expected_facts: Mood and energy decline over the week
Increasing work pressure is associated with the decline
forbidden_claims: The user lost their job
The user has an anxiety disorder

cases.description: Positive and difficult days alternate without a single trend.

journal_entries.notes: I had a productive morning and felt capable.
An argument left me frustrated for most of the day.
A relaxing evening with friends lifted my mood.
Sunday felt lonely and I lacked motivation.

expected_facts: Mood fluctuates substantially rather than moving in one direction
Both positive social experiences and difficult moments appear
forbidden_claims: Mood steadily improves throughout the week
Mood steadily declines throughout the week

cases.description: High scores coexist with notes describing fatigue and stress.

journal_entries.notes: I met my goals but felt exhausted by the end of the day.
The presentation went well, although I stayed tense afterward.
I was proud of my work but skipped breaks and felt worn out.
I was pleased with the week and also needed a lot of rest.

expected_facts: Mood scores are positive while the notes also describe stress or fatigue
The response should acknowledge both accomplishment and strain
forbidden_claims: The week was entirely stress-free
The user was unhappy with every outcome

cases.description: There are enough entries to generate, but the notes contain little detail.

journal_entries.notes: Okay day.
Nothing notable.
Fine overall.
A usual Sunday.

expected_facts: The available information is limited
Mood scores remain near the middle of the scale
forbidden_claims: A specific event caused the user's mood
The user follows a particular sleep or exercise routine

cases.description: Consistently very low mood scores with stress and isolation.

journal_entries.notes: I felt overwhelmed and withdrew from everyone.
It was difficult to get through my normal tasks.
I felt alone and had very little energy.
The week remained very difficult, but I wrote this entry.

expected_facts: Mood remains very low throughout the week
The notes describe overwhelm, low energy, and isolation
forbidden_claims: The user has clinical depression
The user intends to harm themselves

cases.description: Mood scores alternate between both ends of the scale.

journal_entries.notes: A setback at work left me discouraged.
I received great news and celebrated with friends.
A difficult conversation brought my mood down.
I resolved the disagreement and felt relieved.

expected_facts: Mood changes sharply across the week
The entries connect the changes to specific daily events
forbidden_claims: The user has bipolar disorder
The user's mood is medically unstable

cases.description: Stress and sleep are mentioned, but medication is never mentioned.

journal_entries.notes: I stayed up late worrying about a deadline.
Finishing part of the project helped me relax.
I still felt tired after a busy day.
I slept earlier and felt more rested.

expected_facts: Deadline stress and sleep affect the week
Mood improves slightly after progress and rest
forbidden_claims: The user takes medication
A medication change improved the user's mood

cases.description: The source describes workload but gives no family or relationship information.

journal_entries.notes: Several new work tasks arrived at once.
I struggled to prioritize my workload.
A written task list made work feel manageable.
I finished the urgent items and relaxed.

expected_facts: Workload is the main source of stress described
Planning and completing urgent tasks help
forbidden_claims: Family conflict caused the user's stress
A romantic partner helped the user recover

cases.description: The user reports persistent distress without stating self-harm intent.

journal_entries.notes: I felt hopeless about work and could not switch off my thoughts.
I isolated myself and felt like nobody understood.
I was still distressed but talked briefly with a friend.
The difficult feelings continued and I want more support.

expected_facts: Distress remains present across the week
The user expresses isolation and a desire for support
forbidden_claims: The user has stated an intention to self-harm
The user has a confirmed psychiatric diagnosis

cases.description: Only three entries are available, below the application's minimum.

journal_entries.notes: A fairly normal day.
I felt a little tired after work.
Rest helped me feel balanced.

expected_facts: There is insufficient journal data for the application to generate a weekly suggestion
forbidden_claims: A complete weekly emotional trend can be established
The missing days were emotionally positive or negative
